items.raw_snippet: Elon Musk announced the dissolution of xAI, merging it into SpaceX and rebranding it as "SpaceX AI." This move is widely seen as paving the way for SpaceX's historic initial public offering (IPO), with market estimates valuing SpaceX at up to $2 trillion. Concurrently, xAI's core computing asset—the Colossus 1 data center housing over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs—has been entirely leased to rival Anthropic, which recently signed major computing deals with Akamai and Google, seeing its pre-IPO valuation surge to $1.2 trillion. All 12 of xAI's original co-founders have departed, and the Grok model's performance lags behind GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, highlighting the "kill zone" pressure facing closed-source models. items.snippet: # AI drives markets as valuations race ahead of earnings. Is this a legitimate r...
items.raw_snippet: # AI drives markets as valuations race ahead of earnings. Is this a legitimate re-rating of the technology sector, or an overstretched bubble? STOCK markets around the world surged to record highs in April, defying geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and uncertainty over interest rates, as investors crowded into a small group of artificial intelligence and semiconductor giants. In the US, the technology sector contributed nearly 80 per cent of the S&P 500’s estimated 15.1 per cent year-on-year earnings growth in the first quarter. Meanwhile, Hong Kong has become a launchpad for AI startups, pushing fundraising to a five-year high in the first quarter. The enthusiasm has spilled into the primary market, with Chinese venture capital and private equity funding surging past 400 billion yuan (US$59 billion) in the first quarter alone. Yet beneath this coordinated capital rush, a critical debate is emerging: Is this a legitimate re-rating of the technology sector, or an overstretched bubble?

In February, Musk fired back, calling the company “misanthropic and evil.” Musk declared on x then that it was “doomed to this fate when you chose your name,” a jab that doubled as a swipe at OpenAI, whose models are, mostly, well, closed. Musk co-founded OpenAI in 2015 as a nonprofit and is now suing over its transition to a for-profit structure. By May, xAI and Anthropic announced a compute partnership: Anthropic would rent the entirety of xAI’s Colossus 1 data center, over 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs, after SpaceX absorbed xAI in a merger valued at $1.25 trillion and discovered it had more silicon than demand. Musk, meanwhile, departed OpenAI’s board in 2018, called for a moratorium on AI development in 2023, founded xAI weeks later, built one of the largest GPU clusters ever assembled, and is now suing the company he co-founded in a trial playing out in an Oakland courtroom this month.

items.snippet: 高通首席执行官透露OpenAI和Meta正在研发AI可穿戴硬件，标志着大模型向端侧设备渗透加速。
items.raw_snippet: OpenAI logo on a smartphone. ## Qualcomm CEO Says OpenAI, Meta Are Working On AI Wearables That Could Replace Smartphones. **Qualcomm Inc.**(NASDAQ:QCOM) CEO says the smartphone era may be nearing its end as major artificial intelligence companies quietly work on next-generation wearable devices powered by advanced AI agents. Amon described a future centered on what he calls an "ecosystem of you," where devices such as glasses, earbuds and pins continuously collect context from users and allow AI agents to perform tasks automatically. "If AI understands what we say, what we hear, what we see… all of this information is going to be very important context for agents to do things for you," he said. On Wednesday, Qualcomm Chief Executive **Cristiano Amon** said the company is collaborating with "pretty much all" leading AI players, including **OpenAI** and **Meta Platforms** **Inc.** (NASDAQ:META). OpenAI is reportedly developing an AI agent smartphone with Qualcomm and MediaTek, aiming to replace apps with task-driven AI by 2028.

items.raw_snippet: Home » Latest » Thought Leadership » **The AI Boom Is Punishing Slow Companies**. # The AI Boom Is Punishing Slow Companies. The companies still treating it as a side project are no longer being prudent; they are quietly choosing to fall behind. In practical terms, AI is becoming both more capable and cheaper to deploy at the same time. **The Advantage Is Moving From Models To Execution**. For business leaders, as I tell my clients, the most important lesson is that access to AI is no longer the scarce resource. That distinction is showing up in boardrooms and leadership teams where the most practical executives have stopped asking, “What can we do with AI?” and started asking, “Which decisions, workflows, and customer moments should AI improve first?” The clients learning fastest are narrowing the field, choosing a few high-value operating problems, and building the discipline to scale what works.

items.title: Senior Lead Product Manager- Home Lending Agentic AI Transformation, CHARLOTTE, North Carolina / COLUMBUS, Ohio / IRVING, Texas / MINNEAPOLIS, Minnesota + 4 other locations | Wells Fargo
items.snippet: Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Lead Product Manager for Home Lending Originatio...
items.raw_snippet: Wells Fargo is seeking a Senior Lead Product Manager for Home Lending Originations team focused with hands‑on experience driving **agentic process automation**—designing, launching, and scaling intelligent, autonomous workflows that orchestrate people, systems, and data across complex business processes. As a Senior Lead Product Manager, you will lead product strategy and delivery for AI‑enabled, agent‑driven solutions that materially improve speed, accuracy, and customer experience across the end‑to‑end home lending journey, while meeting rigorous regulatory, audit, and risk requirements. The delivery of outcomes will be through ownership of the product backlog inclusive of feature prioritization, transparency into upcoming work, setting of product goals, and communication with stakeholders. * Own product strategy and roadmap for agentic automation capabilities, including autonomous task execution, decision orchestration, exception handling, and human‑in‑the‑loop workflows. * 7+ years of Product Management, product development, strategic planning, process management, change delivery, or agile product owner experience, or equivalent demonstrated through one or a combination of the following: work experience, training, military experience, education.
